subject: research/chip-systolic-p32
professional: a senior computer-architecture researcher / ASIC designer who has built DNN accelerators (the kind who reviews for ISCA, MICRO or IEEE TCAD). They would check first that the RTL is bit-exact and cycle-exact against an independent reference (including saturation paths), that the cycle model matches the textbook output-stationary schedule (Kung 1982; SCALE-Sim's OS model, Samajdar et al. 2018), that the figure of merit is a defensible area-delay product (cells x cycles ignores clock period), and whether the setup can express what a systolic array is for (operand reuse against memory bandwidth) before believing a 'MAC engine wins' result

evidence.correctness: Every number reproduces and recomputes. Full rerun in a scratch copy with the README's tool versions (Yosys 0.33, Icarus 12.0 present here): `cd <copy> && PYTHONPATH=src python3.13 experiments/run.py` took 9 m 04 s and `diff experiments/results.txt <committed>` is empty (byte-identical); `experiments/figure.py` regenerates best_design.svg byte-identically (cmp). Independent recompute (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/08147b7c-603f-5f8a-b9fd-b888a44b0d0f/scratchpad/p32/tools/indep.py, imports nothing from the package): all 20 cycle counts derived from first principles (OS array: operand k reaches PE(r,c) at t=k+r+c, so K+R+C-2 compute + 1 write-back per pass, plus load and transfer; MAC engine: K MACs + 1 write-back per group of P) equal results.txt; all 20 cells x cycles/vec values and both ratios (1.2991 -> 1.30, 1.2786 -> 1.28) recompute; README numbers 0.7% (1-358488/360932=0.68%), 4x8 vs 2x8, 2x16 vs 1x4/2x8 all check. Independent bit-exactness (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/08147b7c-603f-5f8a-b9fd-b888a44b0d0f/scratchpad/p32/tools/rtl_vs_loop.py): a pure-Python loop reference (explicit ReLU, floor shift, clip, not model.int_forward) against the generated RTL in Icarus for MAC P=32/16/8 and arrays 4x8, 2x16, 1x4 at both F=16 and F=32, on 8 test vectors plus 8 adversarial extreme vectors that force 11 and 21 hidden-clip events and 2 output saturations: all match, cycles 36/36/53/83/68/102 and 52/52/85/115/84/166. The tests cover P=32 and 4x8 only at F=16; this confirms F=32 too. Not 4: the F=32 best-design change rests on one synthesis run that the project's own follow-ups (chip-macp32cells, chip-p32netlist) show is a flow artefact, and the headline percentage is misstated (claims).
evidence.completeness: README promises: 6 arrays and 4 MAC engines at F=16 and 32, all 20 RTL simulated against NumPy and the cycle formulas (results.txt has 20 rows, all True; rerun identical), MAC-engine RTL simulated (new here: yes, flow.simulate mac_lanes), tests 'about 1 min' (7 tests OK in 26 s), experiment 'about 15 min' (9 m 04 s), figure from results (figure.py parses results.txt, SVG identical), live page https://marisstella.app/research/chip-systolic-p32/ (HTTP 200, '7 tests', numbers 1.30x/1.28x match). Everything claimed exists and runs end to end; no stubs or TODOs. Next steps (weight-stationary, RAM weights) are listed as not done.
evidence.verification: `cd research/chip-systolic-p32 && PYTHONPATH=src python3.13 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`: Ran 7 tests in 25.9 s, OK (with ResourceWarnings from unclosed files). Six seeded mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py, 1 caught, 5 survived: dropping /R from the headline metric (experiments/run.py:35) survives because no test touches run.py; halving the parsed cell count (flow.py:83) survives because the only area test checks monotonicity; removing the hidden-layer clip in the systolic RTL (gen.py:110) survives because the test vectors never saturate a hidden unit; removing the output QMIN clamp in the MAC RTL (baseline_gen.py:91) and the -8 lower clip in the NumPy spec (model.py:66) both survive. Only the MAC group-loop bound (baseline_gen.py:97 < -> <=) is caught via the cycle check. The parent chip-systolic-hidewide gained flow.metric() and test_metric_divides_by_rows after its 2026-11-13 audit; this copy predates that fix and still has the untested inline metric.
evidence.craft: Read src/chip_systolic_p32/{gen,baseline_gen,flow,model}.py, tests/test_systolic.py, experiments/run.py, experiments/figure.py (613 lines total). Clean small generators, an integer-exact spec, a testbench that checks both outputs and cycles, a figure parsed rather than retyped. Defects: widths() and _rom() duplicated verbatim in gen.py:11/22 and baseline_gen.py:9/19, and baseline_gen.py is byte-identical in 6 research projects (md5 count); stale copied docstrings (baseline_gen.py:3 'fan-in 8 ... 8 MAC cycles', baseline_gen.py:49 'Generated by chip_accel.gen', gen.py:18 'r + c + 6 compute', run.py:2 lists 'R = 1 with C = 4, 8, 16, and R = 2 with C = 8; MAC lanes P = 4, 8, 16', not this sweep); pyproject.toml:6-8 names the package chip-systolic-fanin with a 'Batch-size sweep' description; unclosed file handles (flow.py:45, 46, 74; run.py:17 rewrites the whole results file on every emit); no input validation (a P larger than H builds dead lanes whose ROM index silently wraps to nw bits and which synthesis then removes).
evidence.claims: Checked each Results bullet against results.txt and an independent recompute: table values, 'all 20 simulated designs matched', P=32 = P=16 cycles (36, 52), cell counts 5637/6043 and 6894/6941, 0.7%, 4x8 behind 2x8, 2x16 behind: all backed. Limits and disclaimers are explicit and accurate (one seed, gate counts only, 0.7% not a trend, no fabricated chip). Problems: README:33 'beats the best array by 23% to 30%' mixes two directions; the MAC engine is 23.0% and 21.8% lower (or the array 29.9% and 27.9% higher), so neither end of '23% to 30%' is right for F=32. README:33 'the only change in a best design is P = 32 at F = 32' stands without a pointer to chip-macp32cells/chip-p32netlist, which found that ranking flips with the Yosys flow. The only citation (Kung 1982) is marked 'not read in full', and the nearest prior work is not cited. pyproject.toml describes another project.
evidence.fitness: A researcher can build on the harness: the generators, the bit-exact Icarus check and the Yosys scoring reproduce exactly, and two follow-ups already did build on it (chip-macp32cells, chip-p32netlist, chip-systolic-abcrobust). As a result it is not new: nearest prior work is the output-stationary cycle model of SCALE-Sim (Samajdar et al., arXiv:1811.02883, 2018), the TPU v1 utilisation analysis (Jouppi et al., ISCA 2017) and the dataflow taxonomy of Eyeriss (Chen et al., ISCA 2016), none cited; that a small, skewed R=1..4 array with fill/drain overhead loses to a broadcast MAC engine on 16- and 4-neuron layers with no memory model is what those models predict. Sound within its stated limits (it says negative and stylised), but it is a one-knob extension (P to 32, R to 4) of a chain of near-identical projects rather than a publishable step.
evidence.domain: Compared against standard accelerator-evaluation practice (SCALE-Sim/Timeloop-style cycle models, area-delay product with a real clock, memory-traffic accounting). Departures: weights are compiled into combinational ROM case statements and there is no SRAM or off-array traffic, so the operand reuse a systolic array exists for never enters the metric; the figure of merit is cells x cycles, ignoring the logic depth that results.txt already reports (43-52 vs 38-45 levels); recomputing with cells x cycles x depth widens the array/MAC gap to 1.47 (F=16) and 1.49 (F=32), so the negative result is robust but the metric is not the standard ADP; write-back reads all R*C accumulators in one cycle, where SCALE-Sim's OS model charges an R-cycle drain; generic-gate counts include flip-flops at unit weight. RTL method itself (bit-exact against an integer spec, cycle-exact against a formula) is what a practitioner does.

defects.what: The headline metric, the cell-count parse and every saturation path are untested: 5 of 6 seeded mutants survive (drop /R in run.py:35, halve cells in flow.py:83, remove the hidden clip in gen.py:110, the output QMIN clamp in baseline_gen.py:91, or the -8 clip in model.py:66). The parent chip-systolic-hidewide got flow.metric() and test_metric_divides_by_rows after its audit; this copy was taken before that fix and never received it

The comparison cannot express what a systolic array is for: weights are combinational ROM, there is no memory or traffic model, write-back is one parallel cycle (no OS drain), and the figure of merit omits clock period. The negative result follows from fill/drain on 16- and 4-neuron layers and is what SCALE-Sim / TPU v1 analyses predict; none of that prior work is cited and the only citation is 'not read in full'
'beats the best array by 23% to 30%' mixes directions: MAC is 23.0%/21.8% lower, or the array 29.9%/27.9% higher; neither end is right at F=32

'the only change in a best design is P = 32 at F = 32' has no pointer to the follow-ups (chip-macp32cells, chip-p32netlist) that showed the P=32 vs P=16 ranking flips with the Yosys flow; README runtime 'about 15 min' measured 9 min

verdict: The numbers are right: a full rerun with Yosys 0.33 and Icarus 12.0 reproduces results.txt and the figure byte for byte (9 min), all 20 cycle counts equal the textbook output-stationary and broadcast-MAC schedules derived independently, all 20 cells x cycles values and both ratios recompute, and an independent loop reference matches the RTL bit for bit for P=32, 4x8 and 2x16 at F=32 as well as F=16, including adversarial vectors that drive every saturation path. It does not meet the bar: verification is weak exactly where the result lives (5 of 6 seeded mutants survive, including dropping /R from the headline metric, a defect fixed in the parent project after its audit but not in this copy), the headline '23% to 30%' mixes two directions, and the package metadata and docstrings describe other projects. As research it is a verified RTL harness, not a finding: with ROM weights, no memory, single-cycle write-back and cells x cycles as the merit, the 'MAC engine wins' result is what SCALE-Sim and the TPU v1 analysis predict, and neither is cited. Finished (everything claimed runs) but below the senior-architect bar.
